boundary: src/aee/model.py Claim dataclass and Claim._FIELDS strict-load field set

evidence.description: Claim fields cover text, posture, evidence, falsification tests, stage, and records of acts; no field names how the claim is to be accepted, and strict loading rejects unknown fields.
Grep for acceptance_mode and 'acceptance mode' across src/aee returns zero hits.
evidence.ref: repository grep for acceptance_mode in src/aee, 2026-10-20

falsification_tests: Show an acceptance-mode field on Claim, or an acceptance_mode value accepted by strict loading, in the current model.
claims.text: The claim model carries no acceptance mode: nothing in a bundle records whether a claim is to be accepted by a requirement test, by a named human oracle, or by a gate act, so every acceptance defaults to a recorded human act.

boundary: src/aee/model.py stage machinery on main, and the Spec 006 A4 stage-command rules on branch spec006/lane-outcomes-stage-recording

evidence.description: Spec 006's recorded stage command — the first shipped path for advancing a stage — requires, for accepted and digested, a --recorded-by name that resolves to a person in the identity registry; no test-verdict basis is admitted for any claim.
On main, stage moves only through recorded events whose basis is free text; nothing ties an advance to a test run, a test identity, or a verdict.
evidence.ref: src/aee/model.py Claim.advance_stage and recorded stage events

falsification_tests: Show a shipped command or API by which a recorded test verdict advances a claim to accepted, on main or on the Spec 006 branch.
claims.text: Stage advancement to accepted is gated on a named human for every claim alike: the framework has no recorded path by which a passing requirement test accepts a claim, even when the requirement is purely testable.

boundary: src/aee/model.py EvidenceKind and the Claim falsification_tests field

evidence.description: EvidenceKind has exactly six values — observed, inferred, asserted, contradicted, unsupported, exposition. None carries a test identity, a run record, or a verdict.
Grep for test_verdict, verdict_record, and test_hash across src/aee returns zero hits; falsification_tests load as a list of plain strings.
evidence.ref: repository grep for test_verdict and test_hash in src/aee, 2026-10-20

falsification_tests: Show an evidence kind or record type that carries a test identity and a verdict, or a content hash on a falsification test, in the current model.
claims.text: A test result is not first-class evidence: the evidence kinds are observed, inferred, asserted, contradicted, unsupported, and exposition, and a claim's falsification tests are plain strings with no identity or content hash — so 'the frozen test passed' cannot be recorded in a form the engine can check against the test that was frozen.

boundary: src/aee/model.py bundle schema (Claim and bundle-level fields)

evidence.description: No claim or bundle field carries a restatement, a tripwire set, a discretion envelope, or residual-risk lines; the bundle schema describes claims and their evidence only.
Grep for tripwire and held_out across src/aee returns zero hits.
evidence.ref: repository grep for tripwire and held_out in src/aee, 2026-10-20

falsification_tests: Show bundle fields carrying a restatement, a tripwire set, a discretion envelope, or per-requirement residual-risk lines in the current schema.
claims.text: The planning package the doctrine requires — a restatement, per-requirement acceptance modes, tripwires, a bounded-discretion envelope, and a 'does not establish' line per requirement — has no representation in a claim bundle, so none of it can be recorded, checked at a gate, or sealed in the ledger.

boundary: src/aee assessment serialisation and failure/record categories on main

evidence.ref: src/aee/engine.py assessment record assembly and src/aee/model.py record types

falsification_tests: Show a tripwire event or an assumption record serialised in an assessment produced by the current engine.
claims.text: Execution events have no home in the assessment record: there is no tripwire event and no assumption record, so why a run halted, and what the executor assumed along the way, cannot ride in the record a verdict ships with.

boundary: src/aee/model.py claim model and strict loading; assessment serialisation

claims.text: Every claim in a plan bundle carries an acceptance mode — test, human_oracle, or gate — loaded strictly, and the assessment reports the mode beside the claim's stage and status.

boundary: planning record on the claim; acceptance-time hash comparison

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R2, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Change a frozen test after the planning gate and show the change passing unnoticed — same recorded identity, no mismatch raised — in the acceptance record.
claims.text: A test-mode claim's acceptance test is frozen as an identified, hashed record: the planning record carries the test's identity and content hash, and any later change to the test shows up as a hash mismatch rather than passing as an edit.

boundary: planning-gate validation over the planning record

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R2, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Produce a plan bundle that passed its planning gate with a single derivation, with no deliberate-violation (red) run recorded, or with an unresolved divergence between the two derivations.
claims.text: Each frozen test is derived twice independently and proven able to fail before work begins: the planning record carries both derivations and the deliberate-violation run that turned the test red, and an unresolved divergence between the derivations blocks the planning gate.

boundary: planning record serialisation; acceptance run assembly

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R2 and R6, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Show a held-out check's contents in any bundle, plan, or log an executor reads before acceptance — or produce an acceptance record for a bundle whose held-out checks never ran and were never reported missing.
claims.text: Held-out acceptance checks are recorded by identity and hash only in every executor-visible record; their contents are not serialised into anything the executor can read before acceptance, and at acceptance they run and their verdicts join the record.

boundary: stage-advance rules and assessment cross-checks (Spec 006 A3/A4 machinery, extended)

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R4, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Advance a claim to checked with no frozen able-to-fail test, or to accepted with neither a passing frozen-test verdict (test mode) nor the assigned oracle or gate act, and show the assessment reporting it without a defect.
claims.text: The stage names are re-anchored to the doctrine's definitions — checked means a frozen test exists and has been shown able to fail, explained means the restatement was approved, accepted means the acceptance the plan assigned has happened — and an assessment reports any claim whose stage was advanced on another basis as a defect.

boundary: recorded-act machinery (Spec 006 A4 basis-typed acts, extended); identity registry validation

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R4 and R5, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Advance a human_oracle or gate claim to accepted on a test-verdict act, or a test-mode claim on a verdict whose test hash does not match the frozen hash, and show either recorded without refusal.
claims.text: A recorded act whose basis type is a test verdict — naming the frozen test's identity and hash, the run record, and the delivered artifact's identity — advances a test-mode claim to accepted; a test verdict never advances a human_oracle or gate claim.

boundary: assessment record assembly; outcome logic guard

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R3 and R6, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Halt an execution on a premise tripwire and show the resulting assessment reporting pass, or carrying no tripwire event.
claims.text: Tripwire halts are first-class records: when execution halts, the assessment record carries the tripwire event with its class from the shared halt taxonomy — a premise, equipment, or integrity fault halts everything, while a model's own scored outcome ends only its own run — and no assessment produced after a tripwire halt reports a pass.

boundary: assumption record type; execution-time recording path

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R3, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Run an execution in which the executor records an outcome-changing assumption and continues without a tripwire halt, with the framework raising no defect.
claims.text: Every assumption the executor makes inside its discretion envelope is logged as a record on the affected claim, and an assumption that would change a test's outcome is treated as a tripwire halt, never as discretion.

boundary: acceptance report assembly; completeness checks (Spec 004 R5.3 precedent)

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R6, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Produce an acceptance report that omits a requirement's 'does not establish' line and show it passing the framework's own completeness checks unflagged.
claims.text: The acceptance report is a pair — what the tests established, and every requirement's 'does not establish' line carried verbatim from the plan — and a report missing the second half is flagged the way a missing residual-unknowns statement already is.

evidence.description: Requirement stated in Spec 007 R3 and R7, which this claim commits to test.

falsification_tests: Edit a frozen test in place mid-execution and show the record accepting it without an amendment — or show a light-tier plan whose gate-mode requirement lost its human gate.
claims.text: Frozen things change only by amendment: a change to a frozen test, an acceptance mode, or a tripwire mid-execution is recorded only as a superseding amendment with its own approval act — never as an edit to the frozen record — and plan records carry their proportionality tier and, where used, the exploration-phase marker whose deliverable is a specification.
